editorial:
Imagine starting your year with a quirky guy named Bernard who is obsessed with his scooter. You get swept into his world where the simple joy of riding a moped becomes a way to connect with other people. The vibe is very laid back and sweet, focusing more on the small moments of life rather than a big, loud plot. It feels like you are just hanging out with a group of friends who don't fit in anywhere else, making the whole experience feel warm and welcoming from the very first scene.

What really works here is the natural acting and the slow, steady pace that lets you soak in the atmosphere. While it might feel a bit too quiet for people who love big explosions or fast twists, it is a breath of fresh air if you want something chill. You should definitely check it out if you enjoy character studies. To get the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for those crisp city shots, or you could rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night with your family.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Bernard finally finds a sense of belonging with his fellow scooter lovers. The movie wraps up by showing that his obsession wasn't just about the machine, but about finding a community. He celebrates the Scooter New Year with his new friends, proving that being different is actually what brings people together. It ends on a happy, hopeful note that leaves you feeling good about life.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves quiet stories about friendship and hobbies.
